CVE-2026-76844.why: Flaws in zlib's gzwrite file API; Python's zlib module (used by urllib3/requests for gzip responses) only inflates in memory, and nothing in diyHue writes gz files through zlib. Verified live on hrossen with diyhue/core@sha256:392c1c39 on deconz-test: the container runs only python3 -u HueEmulator3.py --docker as PID 1.

CVE-2026-85091.why: Flaws in zlib's gzwrite file API; Python's zlib module (used by urllib3/requests for gzip responses) only inflates in memory, and nothing in diyHue writes gz files through zlib. Verified live on hrossen with diyhue/core@sha256:392c1c39 on deconz-test: the container runs only python3 -u HueEmulator3.py --docker as PID 1.

CVE-2018-6553.why: Ubuntu's CUPS AppArmor profile for the dnssd backend; NixOS does not ship that profile and no cupsd runs on the VM, libcups is only a transitive Qt5 library of deCONZ.

CVE-2026-63374.why: IDNA 2003 hostname handling in AnyIO TLS connections; anyio is only a dependency of python-kasa's CLI (asyncclick), and diyHue makes no AnyIO TLS connections. (Based on diyHue's published Dockerfile and source, not a live check of the pinned image.)

CVE-2026-44431.why: Cross-origin header forwarding via urllib3 ProxyManager; diyHue's requests calls use no proxy, so ProxyManager is never used. (Based on diyHue's published Dockerfile and source, not a live check of the pinned image.)

CVE-2026-44432.why: urllib3 can fully decompress a response during partial reads; diyHue reads whole responses from LAN light devices it polls or probes, so a malicious device in iotCloud could send a compression bomb and exhaust diyHue's memory. Risk here: low. Action: Bump the pinned diyhue/core digest to a build on a fixed Debian package, re-verifying the bind-mounted deconz.py/Group.py patches.

CVE-2026-97687.why: TLS settings applied to an HTTPS proxy connection; the diyHue container uses no HTTPS proxy.

CVE-2026-97689.why: Unbounded chunk-size line in urllib3's chunked reader; requests reads chunked responses this way, so a malicious HTTP device in the iotCloud zone that diyHue polls or probes during light discovery could exhaust diyHue's memory. Risk here: low. Action: Bump the pinned diyhue/core digest to a build on a fixed Debian package, re-verifying the bind-mounted deconz.py/Group.py patches.
